question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $1-\sqrt{1-2w}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1-\sqrt{1-2w},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{1+\sqrt{1-2w}} & = \\ \frac{2}{1+\sqrt{1-2w}}\cdot \frac{1-\sqrt{1-2w}}{1-\sqrt{1-2w}} & = \\ \frac{2(1-\sqrt{1-2w})}{(1+\sqrt{1-2w})(1-\sqrt{1-2w})} & = \\ \frac{2(1-\sqrt{1-2w})}{{1}^{2}-(\sqrt{1-2w})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{2(1-\sqrt{1-2w})}{1-(1-2w)} & = \\ \frac{2(1-\sqrt{1-2w})}{2w} & = \\ \frac{1-\sqrt{1-2w}}{w}\end{aligned}
$$
